rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both hurried toward the door: Joseph to flee, while the wife pursued him.
rows.anchor: أي أسرعا إليه , أما يوسف فأسرع إليه هربا , وأما امرأة العزيز فأسرعت إليه طلبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She caught Joseph after he had opened some locks, grabbed him from behind, and tore his shirt down to his shin.
rows.anchor: أدركته وقد فتح بعض الأغلاق فجذبته من ورائه فشقت قميصه إلى ساقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph's shirt fell off as she pursued him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وسقط عنه وتبعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Her master” means her husband.
rows.anchor: أي وجدا زوجها عند الباب

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the word “master” means husband in Coptic.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح : والسيد هو الزوج بلسان القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife accused Joseph to her husband to divert suspicion from herself and put it on him.
rows.anchor: لتدفع الريبة عن نفسها بإلقائها على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her love was mixed with lust: desire made her protect herself by lying; without lust, she would have protected Joseph by telling the truth.
rows.anchor: اقترن شدة حبها بالشهوة طلبت دفع الضرر بالتكذيب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph answered truthfully because she had first falsely exonerated herself; had she not lied, he would have stayed silent.
rows.anchor: لما برأت نفسها بالكذب عليه احتاج أن يبرىء نفسه بالصدق عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “witness” was a judge from her family: their claims conflicted, so the king needed a ruling to distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: حكم حاكم من أهلها لأنه حكم منه وليس شهادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك
rows.claim: One view identifies the witness as an infant whom God enabled to speak in the cradle.
rows.anchor: أنه صبي أنطقه الله تعالى في مهده , قاله ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One of Mujahid's views identifies the witness as a creature of God who was neither human nor jinn.
rows.anchor: أنه خلق من خلق الله تعالى ليس بإنس ولا جن , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the witness as a wise man from the wife's family.
rows.anchor: أنه رجل حكيم من أهلها , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the wise witness was her cousin.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وكان ابن عمها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies the witness as the testimony supplied by the torn shirt itself.
rows.anchor: أنه عنى شهادة القميص المقدود , قاله مجاهد أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A front tear would show Joseph had approached her; a back tear would show he was fleeing from her.
rows.anchor: إذا طلب المرأة كان مقبلا عليها فيكون شق قميصه من قبله دليلا على طلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's shirt is one of three signs: its back tear proved him truthful, the false blood on it exposed his brothers, and its placement on Jacob's face restored his sight.
rows.anchor: وهذه إحدى الآيات الثلاث في قميصه : إن كان قد من دبر فكان فيه دليل على صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the back tear established Joseph's truth, so the speaker affirmed that it was the women's plotting.
rows.anchor: علم بذلك صدق يوسف فصدقه وقال إنه من كيدكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Plotting” here can mean either the wife's lie against Joseph or the evil she had invited him to do.
rows.anchor: وفي الكيد هما وجهان : أحدهما : يعني به كذبها عليه . الثاني : أنه أراد السوء

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the husband spoke the words about the women's plotting.
rows.anchor: أنه الزوج , قاله محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa transmits the alternative that the witness spoke the words about the women's plotting.
rows.anchor: أنه الشاهد , حكاه علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads “Joseph, turn away from this” as consolation, assuring him that he bears no sin.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن هذا الأمر , قال قتادة : على وجه التسلية له في ارتفاع الإثم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads it as telling Joseph to disregard the wife's accusation, affirming his innocence.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن هذا القول , قاله ابن زيد على وجه التصديق له في البراءة من الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king told his wife to seek forgiveness for her sin; he was also the speaker who told Joseph to turn away.
rows.anchor: هذا قول الملك لزوجه وهو القائل ليوسف أعرض عن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for the husband's silence is that he was not jealous.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يكن غيورا فلذلك كان ساكتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God removed the husband's jealousy as a kindness to Joseph, enabling him to restrain himself and order his wife to repent and stop.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى سلبه الغيرة وكان فيه لطف بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One of the sinners” denotes someone who intentionally sins; the related form for an unintended mistake is أخطأ.
rows.anchor: يقال لمن قصد الذنب خطىء , ولمن لم يقصده أخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural الخاطئين is used instead of the feminine الخاطئات because masculine forms conventionally include or prevail over feminine forms; the preceding poet's line uses خطئي وصوبي.
rows.anchor: وقال من الخاطئين ولم يقل من الخاطئات لتغليب المذكر على المؤنث

rows.speaker: جويبر
rows.claim: Juwair says the women were four: the doorkeeper's wife, the cupbearer's wife, the baker's wife, and the steward's wife.
rows.anchor: قال جويبر : كن أربعا : امرأة الحاجب وامرأة الساقي وامرأة الخباز وامرأة القهرمان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil adds the prison keeper's wife to the women in the city.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : وامرأة صاحب السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is identified either as Egypt or as Ain Shams.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه المدينة قولان : أحدهما : مصر . الثاني : عين شمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women spoke to shame the wife of al-Aziz, vindicate Joseph, and deny that he was guilty.
rows.anchor: قلن ذلك ذما لها وطعنا فيها وتحقيقا لبراءة يوسف وإنكارا لذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz is a royal title derived from might; Abu Dawud's verse uses عزيز in this sense.
rows.anchor: والعزيز اسم الملك مأخوذ من عزته , ومنه قول أبى داؤد

rows.speaker: أبو داؤد
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's cited line includes عزيز, witnessing the royal title or its sense of might.
rows.anchor: جلبت عند عزيز يوم طل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Her love penetrated her shighaf” means it entered the heart's shighaf.
rows.anchor: أي قد دخل حبه من شغاف قلبها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the heart's shighaf as its veil.
rows.anchor: أنه حجاب القلب , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي وسفيان
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Sufyan define shighaf as the heart's covering, a thin white skin also called its garment.
rows.anchor: أنه غلاف القلب وهو جلدة رقيقة بيضاء تكون على القلب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan defines shighaf as the heart's interior; another gloss in this group calls it the heart's core.
rows.anchor: أنه باطن القلب , قاله الحسن , وقيل هو حبة القلب

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i glosses shighaf as what is inside the body cavity.
rows.anchor: أنه ما يكون في الجوف , قاله الأصمعي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says shighaf is the alarm and panic caused by intense love.
rows.anchor: هو الذعر والفزع الحادث عن شدة الحب , قاله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: An anomalous reading attributed to Ibn Muhaysin reads شعفها with an unpointed ع instead of غ.
rows.anchor: قد شعفها حبا ( بالعين غير معجمة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi distinguishes the readings by saying شغف with غ means madness, while شعف with ع means love.
rows.anchor: أن الشغف بالغين معجمة هو الجنون وبالعين غير معجمة هو الحب , قاله الشعبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas offers another distinction: شغف with غ is love that kills, while شعف with ع is less intense.
rows.anchor: أن الشغف بالإعجام الحب القاتل , والشعف بغير إعجام دونه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhu'ayb's cited verse uses شغاف القلب to attest the word's association with the heart.
rows.anchor: أصاب شغاف القلب والقلب يشغف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Manifest error” may mean straying from right guidance and truth, or it may mean intense love.
rows.anchor: في ضلال عن الرشد وعدول عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As above, intense love combined with lust made the wife protect herself by lying; without lust she would have protected Joseph with the truth.
rows.anchor: اقترن شدة حبها بالشهوة طلبت دفع الضرر عن نفسها بالكذب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their plotting” may be the women's disparagement of the wife and criticism of her conduct.
rows.anchor: أنه ذمهن لها وإنكارهن عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, she had privately told the women she loved Joseph and they spread that confidence.
rows.anchor: أنها أسرت إليهن بحبها له فأشعن ذلك عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form أعتدت may derive either from preparing something or from aggression.
rows.anchor: وفي { أعتدت } وجهان : أحدهما : أنه من الإعداد . الثاني : أنه من العدوان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan gloss mutta'aka as a sitting place or gathering.
rows.anchor: أنه المجلس , قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والسدي
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Suddi gloss mutta'aka as cushions or pillows on which guests recline.
rows.anchor: أنه النمارق والوسائد يتكأ عليها , قاله أبو عبيدة والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third gloss is food: Arabs say they “reclined at someone's” to mean they ate there, and the prepared seat gave its name to the meal by metaphor.
rows.anchor: أنه الطعام مأخوذ من قول العرب اتكأنا عند فلان أي طعمنا عنده

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd identify the food as zamawarda, a spiced dish.
rows.anchor: أنه الزماورد , قاله الضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify it as citron; this is also the interpretation tied to the unhamzated light reading متك.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word المتك means citron.
rows.anchor: والمتك في كلامهم الأترج

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses المتك for citron and الإثم for wine.
rows.anchor: نشرب الإثم بالصواع جهارا … وترى المتك بيننا متسعارا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the food was anything cut with a knife, since it is commonly eaten while seated.
rows.anchor: أنه كل ما يجز بالسكين وهو قول عكرمة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatada take the word broadly to mean all food and drink.
rows.anchor: أنه كل الطعام والشراب على عمومه , وهو قول سعيد بن جبير وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knives ostensibly helped the women eat; secretly, they were intended to make their amazement visible as evidence against them.
rows.anchor: في الظاهر معونة على الأكل , وفي الباطن ليظهر من دهشتهن ما يكون شاهدا عليهن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Joseph was like her servant, so she would not allow him to appear without her order.
rows.anchor: كان كالعبد لها فلم تمكنه أن يخرج إلا بأمرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses أكبرنه as “they greatly admired him.”
rows.anchor: معناه أعظمنه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr glosses it as their finding his beauty and bearing extraordinary.
rows.anchor: وجدن شأنه في الحسن والجمال كبيرا , قال ابن بحر

rows.speaker: عبد الصمد بن علي الهاشمي
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abd al-Samad ibn Ali al-Hashimi from his father, from Ibn Abbas, interprets أكبرنه as menstruating at Joseph's sight; fear or distress could cause it, and menstruation could be called ikbar.
rows.anchor: معناه : حضن عند رؤيته , وهو قول رواه عبد الصمد بن علي الهاشمي عن أبيه عن جده عبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the food was received in a dream, and Joseph would interpret it before they awoke.
rows.anchor: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه في النوم إلا نبأتكما بتأويله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the food was in waking life; Joseph told them its meaning before it reached them, as he could report hidden matters like Jesus.
rows.anchor: في اليقظة إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يصلكما لأنه كان يخبر بما غاب مثل عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the king customarily sent a particular meal before executing someone; Joseph delayed interpreting their bad dreams until its arrival so as not to frighten them, then explained them when they pressed him.
rows.anchor: الملك كان من عادته إذا أراد قتل إنسان صنع له طعاما معروفا وأرسل به إليه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reports from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet said a dream should be told only to a beloved person or someone wise; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is from what my Lord taught me” refers to interpreting dreams.
rows.anchor: ذلكما مما علمنى ربي } يعني تأويل الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph redirected the conversation from their question because dream interpretation was an honor, then declared his rejection of their unbelieving religion to affirm his steadfastness and urge worship of God.
rows.anchor: عدل عن تأويل ما سألاه عنه لما كان فيها من الكرامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's favor to Joseph was making him a prophet, and His favor to people was sending them messengers.
rows.anchor: من فضل الله علينا أن جعلنا أنبياء , وعلى الناس أن بعثنا إليهم رسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that God favored Joseph by keeping him free of adultery and favored people by freeing them from the sin of falsely accusing him.
rows.anchor: في أن برأنا من الزنى , وعلى الناس من أن خلصهم من مأثم القذف

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses al-din al-qayyim as the straight religion.
rows.anchor: ذلك الدين المستقيم , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses it as the clear reckoning.
rows.anchor: الحساب البين , قاله مقاتل بن حيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as the true judgment.
rows.anchor: يعني القضاء الحق , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view assigns “I do not absolve myself” to al-Aziz: he does not clear himself of suspecting Joseph.
rows.anchor: أنه قول العزيز أي وما أبرىء نفسي من سوء الظن بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the al-Aziz reading, “the soul commands evil” may mean it urges suspicion or makes accusations when doubts arise.
rows.anchor: الأمارة بسوء الظن . الثاني : بالاتهام عند الارتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, God’s mercy may keep the speaker from suspicion or restrain him so he does not act.
rows.anchor: إلا ما رحم ربي إن كفاه سوء الظن . الثاني : أن يثنيه حتى لا يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view assigns the words to the wife, who does not absolve herself if she solicited Joseph, since lust makes the soul command evil.
rows.anchor: أنه قول امرأة العزيز وما أبرىء نفسي إن كنت راودت يوسف عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the wife's reading, God's mercy may mean removing her desire or overpowering her own desire.
rows.anchor: إلا ما رحم ربي من نزع شهوته منه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the exchange followed Joseph's statement that he had not betrayed the absent master: the wife challenged whether he had done so when he removed his trousers.
rows.anchor: فقال : وما أبريء نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء ، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel reproached Joseph after his statement of innocence, asking whether he had done so when he intended the act.
rows.anchor: فقال { وما أبريء نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the angel accompanying Joseph told him to remember what he had intended.
rows.anchor: فقال : { وما أبرىء نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Joseph disliked praising himself after saying he had not betrayed the absent master, so he added that he did not absolve his soul.
rows.anchor: فقال { وما أبريء نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible sense of “the soul commands evil” is that it inclines toward desire and urges wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: يعني أنها مائلة إلى الهوى بالأمر بالسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that the soul finds weighty duties burdensome and, without resolve, this leads to evil.
rows.anchor: تستثقل من عزائم الأمور ما إن لم يصادف حزما أفضت إلى السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After learning Joseph's trustworthiness, the greater king summoned him and chose him for his private service.
rows.anchor: لما علم أمانة يوسف اختاره ليستخلصه لنفسه في خاص خدمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king inferred Joseph's intelligence from his speech and trustworthiness from his chastity.
rows.anchor: استدل بكلامه على عقله , وبعصمته على أمانته

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses makin as dignified or held in high regard.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { مكين } وجهان : أحدهما : وجيه , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss of makin is firmly established in an elevated rank.
rows.anchor: متمكن في المنزلة الرفيعة

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara glosses amin as safe from feared consequences.
rows.anchor: أنه بمعنى آمن لا تخاف العواقب , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn Isa glosses amin as trustworthy and reliable.
rows.anchor: أنه بمعنى مأمون ثقة , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses amin as a keeper or guardian.
rows.anchor: الثالث : حافظ , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Treasuries of the land” refers to the treasuries of the king's land.
rows.anchor: أي على خزائن أرضك

rows.speaker: بعض المتعمقة
rows.claim: A speculative group interprets the treasuries as people, since people's deeds and speech are stored in them.
rows.anchor: أن الخزائن ها هنا الرجال , لأن الأفعال والأقوال مخزونة فيهم

rows.speaker: أصحاب الظاهر
rows.claim: The apparentist view takes the treasuries to mean stores of wealth.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أصحاب الظاهر أنها خزائن الأموال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Joseph asked for all the treasuries.
rows.anchor: أنه سأله جميع الخزائن , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: شيبة بن نعامة الضبي
rows.claim: Shayba ibn Nu'ama al-Dabbi says Joseph asked for the food stores.
rows.anchor: أنه سأله خزائن الطعام , قاله شيبة بن نعامة الضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qualified person may seek an office whose duties and conditions he can fulfill.
rows.anchor: دليل على جواز أن يخطب الإنسان عملا يكون له أهلا وهو بحقوقه وشروطه قائم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin transmits Abu Hurayra's account that Umar removed him from Bahrain's office, then called him back; when he refused, Umar asked why, since Joseph had sought office.
rows.anchor: حكى ابن سيرين عن أبي هريرة قال : نزعني عمر بن الخطاب عن عمل البحرين ثم دعاني إليها فأبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One legal view allows serving an unjust ruler if the official acts justly, since Joseph served Pharaoh and responsibility rests on one's own conduct.
rows.anchor: جوازها إن عمل بالحق فيما تقلده , لأن يوسف عليه السلام ولي من قبل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposing view forbids it because it assists oppressors and lends legitimacy to their rule.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز ذلك له لما فيه من تولي الظالمين بالمعونة لهم وتزكيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says Joseph's Pharaoh was righteous; only Moses' Pharaoh was tyrannical.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون يوسف كان صالحا , وإنما الطاغي فرعون موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says Joseph managed the ruler's property, not his governmental offices, avoiding complicity in his rule.
rows.anchor: أنه نظر له في أملاكه دون أعماله فزالت عنه التبعة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes three cases: handling prescribed charitable dues without discretion may be allowed under an unjust ruler.
rows.anchor: ما يجوز لأهله فعله من غير اجتهاد في تنفيذه كالصدقات والزكوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Managing funds that require discretionary allocation, such as fay, is impermissible under an unjust ruler because it entails unauthorized disposal.
rows.anchor: ما لا يجوز أن يتفردوا به ويلزم الإجتهاد في مصرفه كأموال الفيء فلا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For duties that are lawful but involve discretion, such as judgments, appointment is conditional: enforcing an agreed judgment or mediating may be allowed, while coercive enforcement is not.
rows.anchor: ما يجوز أن يتولاه أهله وللاجتهاد فيه مدخل كالقضايا والأحكام

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses حفيظ عليم as preserving what was entrusted and knowing what was assigned.
rows.anchor: حفيظ لما استودعتني عليم بما وليتني , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن سراقة
rows.claim: Ibn Suraqa transmits the gloss “keeper by writing, knowledgeable in accounting,” adding that Joseph was the first to write on papyrus.
rows.anchor: حفيظ بالكتاب , عليم بالحساب , حكاه ابن سراقة , وأنه أول من كتب في القراطيس

rows.speaker: الأشجع عن سفيان
rows.claim: Al-Ashja'i reports from Sufyan the gloss “keeper of accounts, knowledgeable in languages.”
rows.anchor: حفيظ بالحساب , عليم بالألسن , قاله الأشجع عن سفيان

rows.speaker: قتادة وشيبة الضبي
rows.claim: Qatada glosses حفيظ as guarding the office; Shayba says عليم means knowledgeable about the famine years.
rows.anchor: حفيظ لما وليتني , قاله قتادة , عليم بسني المجاعة , قاله شيبة الضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may describe relevant ability and merit, but unrestricted self-description risks self-purification and ostentation; restraint suits the virtuous, while Joseph had an urgent need and hoped to save his people.
rows.anchor: يجوز للإنسان أن يصف نفسه بما فيه من علم وفضل , وليس هذا على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the great king al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan appointed Joseph over Ifir's post and removed Ifir.
rows.anchor: استخلصه الملك الأكبر الوليد بن الريان على عمل إظفير وعزله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Ifir accepted Islam under Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : وأسلم على يده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph became king after a year and a half.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ملك بعد سنة ونصف

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil reports that the Prophet said Joseph would have become king at that time had he qualified his claim to be a capable keeper with “God willing”; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: لو أن يوسف قال : إني حفيظ عليم إن شاء الله لملك في وقته ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Ifir died, the king married Joseph to Ifir's wife Ra'il; Joseph found her a virgin, and she bore him Ephraim and Manasseh.
rows.anchor: ثم مات إظفير فزوجه الملك بامرأة إظفير راعيل , فدخل بها يوسف فوجدها عذراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who identify the woman as Zulaykha say Joseph did not marry her: after seeing his procession, she praised God for making disobedient kings servants and obedient servants kings, and he kept her in his household until her death.
rows.anchor: ومن زعم أنها زليخا قال لم يتزوجها يوسف وأنها لما رأته في موكبه بكت

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Joseph took a residence wherever he wished in Egypt.
rows.anchor: يتخذ من أرض مصر منزلا حيث يشاء , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says Joseph could do whatever he wished in the world because authority had been entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: يصنع في الدنيا ما يشاء لتفويض الأمر إليه , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy and favor here refer to worldly mercy and blessing.
rows.anchor: نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء } يعني في الدنيا بالرحمة والنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We do not let the reward of the good be lost” refers to their recompense in the afterlife; others apply it to this world, but the author prefers the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يعني في الآخرة بالجزاء . ومنهم من حملها على الدنيا , ومنهم من حملها على الآخرة , والأصح ما قدمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats Joseph's prosperity as God's reward for his trials.
rows.anchor: ثواب من الله تعالى على ما ابتلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats it as a gracious gift, with Joseph's reward still awaiting him in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أنه أنعم بذلك عليه تفضلا منه , وثوابه باق على حاله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's reward is better than worldly reward because it lasts while this world passes away.
rows.anchor: لأن أجر الآخرة دائم , وأجر الدنيا منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the afterlife reward is better for Joseph than occupying himself with worldly kingship and pleasure, which carry liability.
rows.anchor: خير ليوسف من التشاغل بملك الدنيا ونعيمها لما فيه من التبعة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi say the brothers came to buy grain from Egypt during the famine years Joseph had predicted.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاءوا ليمتاروا من مصر في سني القحط التي ذكرها يوسف في تفسير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They entered Joseph's presence because he personally oversaw grain sales due to its scarcity.
rows.anchor: دخلوا على يوسف لأنه كان هو الذي يتولى بيع الطعام لعزته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph recognized his brothers as soon as they entered.
rows.anchor: أنه عرفهم حين دخلوا عليه من غير تعريف , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Joseph recognized them only after they introduced themselves.
rows.anchor: ما عرفهم حتى تعرفوا إليه فعرفهم , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph recognized his brothers when he heard them speak Hebrew.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل عرفهم بلسانهم العبراني حين تكلموا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “Hebrew” by saying Abraham crossed with them into Palestine and settled beyond the Jordan, so they were called Hebrews.
rows.anchor: إنما سميت عبرانية لأن إبراهيم عليه السلام عبر بهم فلسطين فنزل من وراء نهر الأردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not recognize Joseph because he had been a child and poor when they left him, but was now grown, wealthy, and a king; he concealed his identity.
rows.anchor: فارقوه صغيرا فكبر , وفقيرا فاستغنى , وباعوه عبدا فصار ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph measured grain for them; Ibn Ishaq says each man received a camel load according to his allotment.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه كال لهم الطعام , قال ابن إسحاق : وحمل لكل رجل منهم بعيرا بعدتهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the requested paternal brother as Benjamin, Joseph's full brother.
rows.anchor: يعني بنيامين وكان أخا يوسف لأبيه وأمه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph admitted them, declared his suspicion that they might be spies, and asked their identity; after hearing about their father, Joseph, and the absent brother, he asked them to bring him to verify their account.
rows.anchor: قد استربت بكم تنكر عليهم فأخبروني من أنتم فإني أخاف أن تكونوا عيونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, after the brothers described Benjamin as especially beloved by their father, Joseph pretended he wished to see him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بل وصفوا له أنه أحب إلى أبيهم منهم , فأظهر لهم محبة رؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you not see that I give full measure?” may mean Joseph lowered the price, increasing what the measure bought, or that he filled the measure properly.
rows.anchor: أنه أرخص لهم في السعر فصار زيادة في الكيل . الثاني : أنه كال لهم بمكيال واف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “I am the best host” as the best person to provide hospitality.
rows.anchor: يعني خير المضيفين , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph means he is the most trustworthy person with whom they have stayed; the wording can refer to food or lodging.
rows.anchor: خير من نزلتم عليه من المأمونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No measure for you with me” threatens to deny future grain, since Joseph had already given them their measure on this visit.
rows.anchor: يعني فيما بعد لأنه قد وفاهم كيلهم في هذه الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not come near me” means he will not treat them as close, not that they may never return, since he urged them to come back.
rows.anchor: أي لا أنزلكم عندي منزلة القريب . ولم يرد أن يبعدوا منه ولا يعودوا إليه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph demanded a hostage and detained Simeon.
rows.anchor: وطلب منهم رهينة حتى يرجعوا , فارتهن شمعون عنده

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Simeon was chosen because at the well he had spoken most handsomely and shown the best judgment.
rows.anchor: إنما اختار شمعون منهم لأنه يوم الجب كان أجملهم قولا وأحسنهم رأيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muraawada means earnest effort in seeking, and the word derives from irada, “will.”
rows.anchor: والمراودة الاجتهاد في الطلب , مأخوذ من الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will do it” may mean they will strive to persuade their father and request Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وإنا لفاعلون مراودة أبيه وطلبه منه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reads “we will do it” as a promise to return to Joseph with their brother.
rows.anchor: وإنا لفاعلون للعود إليه بأخيهم , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grief caused by Joseph's demand may have been God's commanded trial of Jacob, increasing his eventual reward.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الله عز وجل أمره بذلك ابتلاء ليعقوب ليعظم له الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph intended to alert Jacob to Joseph's situation.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون أراد بذلك أن ينبه يعقوب على حال يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, having both sons return would multiply Jacob's joy.
rows.anchor: لتضاعف المسرة ليعقوب برجوع ولديه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph wanted his full brother to enjoy reunion with him before the other brothers, because of their closeness.
rows.anchor: ليقدم سرور أخيه بالاجتماع معه قبل إخوته لميله إليه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read لفتيانه; two explanations follow for who Joseph's men were.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { لفتيانه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the men called fityan were Joseph's servants.
rows.anchor: أنهم غلمانه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they were the men who had measured the grain for the brothers.
rows.anchor: أنهم الذين كالوا لهم الطعام , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' returned goods may have been their currency, or eight bags of meal made from the desert colocynth.
rows.anchor: أنها ورقهم التي ابتاعوا الطعام بها . الثاني : أنها كانت ثمانية جرب فيها سويق المقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars see the returned goods as a sign that people's deeds return to them as reward for obedience or punishment for sin.
rows.anchor: نبه الله تعالى برد بضاعتهم إليهم على أن أعمال العباد تعود إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that they may know it” means “so that they may recognize it.”
rows.anchor: لعلهم يعرفونها } أي ليعرفوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When they returned to their family” means when they went back; the same wording appears in 3:174.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ^ { فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله } ^ [ آل عمران : 174 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that they may return” states Joseph's purpose: that they come back.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون } أي ليرجعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may have returned their payment simply to encourage them to return, as he said openly.
rows.anchor: ترغيبا لهم ليرجعوا , على ما صرح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have known they would not keep the money and would return to tell him they had found it.
rows.anchor: أنه علم منهم لا يستحلون إمساكها , وأنهم يرجعون لتعريفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have wanted them to know his request for their return was not greed for their money.
rows.anchor: ليعلموا أنه لم يكن طلبه لعودهم طمعا في أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have feared that famine had left their father with no other provisions.
rows.anchor: أنه خشي أن لا يكون عند أبيه غيرها للقحط الذي نزل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have felt scrupulous about taking payment for his family's food while they were in great need.
rows.anchor: أنه تحرج أن يأخذ من أبيه وإخوته ثمن قوتهم مع شدة حاجتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's family camp was placed either at al-Arabat in Palestine or at al-Awlaj near al-Sha'b below Hims; the latter view describes Jacob as a nomad with sheep and camels.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : بالعربات من أرض فلسطين . الثاني : بالأولاج من ناحية الشعب أسفل من حمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers meant that the king would deny them grain on a return without Benjamin, since he required his presence either to see him or verify their truthfulness.
rows.anchor:
سيمنع منا الكيل إن عدنا 
بغير أخينا لأن ملك مصر ألزمنا به وطلبه منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Send our brother with us, so we may measure” means they could return to Joseph and obtain grain if Benjamin went with them.
rows.anchor: أي إن أرسلته معنا أمكننا أن نعود إليه ونكتال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to protect Benjamin was meant to persuade Jacob to send him.
rows.anchor: ترغيبا له في إرساله معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob distrusted them because they had pledged to protect Joseph and then lost him.
rows.anchor: لأنهم ضمنوا له حفظ يوسف فأضاعوه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read حافظا, meaning God is a better protector than the brothers.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { حافظا } يعني منكم لأخيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is the most merciful of the merciful” may mean most merciful in guarding what is entrusted.
rows.anchor: أرحم الراحمين في حفظ ما استودع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean most merciful toward Jacob in his visible grief.
rows.anchor: أرحم الراحمين فيما يرى من حزني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The returned goods were the payment they had given for the grain they bought.
rows.anchor: وجدوا التي كانت بضاعتهم وهو ما دفعوه في ثمن الطعام الذي امتاروه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads ما نبغي as a question: what more could they want after the king's treatment of them?
rows.anchor: على وجه الاستفهام بمعنى ما نبغي بعد هذا الذي قد عاملنا به , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn Isa explains it as saying they had no reason to lie about what they had told Jacob of the king.
rows.anchor: معناه ما نبغي بالكذب فيما أخبرناك به عن الملك , حكاه ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This is our payment returned to us” may inform Jacob of what happened or encourage him; encouragement is the stronger reading.
rows.anchor: احتمل أن يكون قولهم ذلك له تعريفا واحتمل أن يكون ترغيبا , وهو أظهر الاحتمالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namiru means to bring provisions; al-mira is food that sustains people.
rows.anchor: أي نأتيهم بالميرة , وهي الطعام المقتات

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses مائرا for someone sent to bring provisions.
rows.anchor: بعثتك مائرا فمكثت حولا متى يأتي غياثك من تغيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to bring provisions was pure persuasion aimed at Jacob.
rows.anchor: هذا ترغيب محض ليعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to protect Benjamin was an attempt to soften Jacob's resistance.
rows.anchor: وهذا استنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra camel measure may be the load carried by Benjamin, or Benjamin's own ration, since Yusuf allotted each person only a camel load.
rows.anchor: كيل البعير نحمل عليه أخانا . والثاني : كيل بعير هو نصيب أخينا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says “that is a small measure” means the amount they brought was too little to benefit them, an appeal for sympathy.
rows.anchor: أن الذي جئناك به كيل يسير لا ينفعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the requested amount was easy for the person measuring it, a way of making their request seem simple.
rows.anchor: أن ما نريده يسير على من يكيل لنا , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers fulfilled their promise to keep pressing Joseph for Benjamin, trying persuasion, softening, appeal, and making the request easy.
rows.anchor: قد راودوه من سائر جهات المراودة ترغيبا واستنزالا واستعطافا وتسهيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's divine pledge may mean they called God to witness against themselves.
rows.anchor: أنه إشهادهم الله على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the pledge was an oath sworn by God.
rows.anchor: أنه حلفهم بالله , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view takes the pledge to mean that someone guaranteed or stood surety for them.
rows.anchor: أنه كفيل يتكفل بهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “unless you are encompassed” as “unless all of you are destroyed.”
rows.anchor: يعني إلا أن يهلك جميعكم , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the exception as their being overpowered and losing control of their situation.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تغلبوا على أمركم , قاله قتادة
